conviction_note: Event and 15:30 release confirmed; H1 should land on or slightly above the 22.0bn OP plan on a weaker yen (FX tailwind offset by renewed oil/energy cost and a weak 中食 segment), the FY guide decision is a coin flip between hold and a cautious trim, and the one asymmetric item is a possible repeat of last year's H1 buyback, so p_up 52 on abs 2.5 gives +0.1 while the findings sum to +0.4; the gap is small and both say there is no strong edge.
bar: Company H1 guide OP 22.0bn / ordinary 23.0bn, FY OP 46.0bn / ordinary 49.0bn, unchanged since 2026-05-14 (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260730/140120260729502339.pdf); IFIS consensus H1 ordinary 23.0bn, FY OP 46.67bn / ordinary 49.67bn / NP 39.33bn, flat for four weeks (https://kabuyoho.jp/reportAnalyst?bcode=2002, read 2026-10-28). Two sources agree the street sits on or a touch above plan.
positioning_check: JPX disclosed short register: 0.0% (no position >=0.5%), no change, as of 2026-10-27 (baseline, https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html). 信用倍率 0.90 (margin shorts slightly exceed margin longs; also shown on https://kabutan.jp/stock/?code=2002 on 2026-10-28). No skew exists. run_up_20d +3.25% (stock rallied from 1,954 on 10-02 to 2,098.5 on 10-26) but -1.4% on 10-27 and about -1.5% intraday on 10-28 into the print. priced_lean -0.14.

findings.finding: Q2 (Jul-Sep 2026) yen was weaker than the plan's FX assumptions: USD/JPY month-end ~160.1/157.4/156.9 vs plan 155.0 and AUD/JPY ~114.6/110.0/110.3 vs plan 105.0, on an overseas business planned at 17.4bn OP (37.8% of group) whose Q1 OP rose 24.6% with 0.5bn of FX translation; this supports H1 landing on or slightly above the 22.0bn OP guide (Q2 needs 10.8bn vs 11.34bn a year ago).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026-07-30: in-line quarter (OP -0.9%, '当社想定に沿って進捗', guide held) and the stock fell 4.78% the next session; the market has not rewarded in-line quarters on this name recently.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: FX is public and IFIS consensus already sits 1.4% above the company FY OP. What is not visible is how much of the translation gain survives Middle East cost; if the market had fully priced an H1 beat the stock would not have sold 4.8% on an in-line Q1 and would carry consensus H1 above plan rather than equal to it (23.0bn = plan).
findings.independence: FX series from Yahoo (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/JPY=X?range=1y&interval=1mo); same 補足資料 gives the plan rates. Partly one document.

findings.finding: Cost pressure re-accelerated after the guide was set: Brent rose from ~90 in Jul-Aug to ~103.5 at end-Sep and ~111-117 in October, and MAFF raised the October imported-wheat sale price 12.0% citing Middle East freight, with pass-through only from 2027-01 deliveries (Welna announced 2026-10-21), so the H2 cost lag is a reason for the company to trim or hedge the FY guide at this print as it did at last year's H1 (2025-10-30 OP cut 6%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 2025-10-30: OP guide cut 6% with India impairment and a 20bn buyback, stock -1.61%; H1 2024-10-30: NP raised 3% and dividend +5, stock -1.03%; H1 2023 (10-27): large upgrade, stock jumped. Revisions at the H1 print happened three years running.
findings.why_not_priced: Oil and the wheat price are public, so the cost itself is held; what is not resolved is the company's decision. The May guide explicitly built in Middle East cost risk and the tanshin promised to revise 'if needed', so a hold is as likely as a trim; a fully priced cut would show consensus below the company plan, and it sits above.
findings.independence: Oil series https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/BZ=F?range=1y&interval=1mo; Welna price hike https://news.nissyoku.co.jp/flash/1329215 (2026-10-21); FY guide wording https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260514/140120260513530641.pdf

findings.finding: A new buyback at this H1 print is plausible: last year's H1 (2025-10-30) carried a 20bn / 5.18% trust buyback, that programme finished in April 2026, the FY tanshin says '財務状況等を踏まえ、更なる株主還元も検討', NP guide 41bn is lifted by further 政策保有株式 sales and asset sales that generate cash, and Mizuho Bank has been selling its stake (below 5% on 2026-10-07), supply a buyback would absorb.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-10-30: 20bn buyback announced alongside a guidance cut and impairment, stock still -1.61%; 2024-10-30: +5 yen dividend with a small NP raise, stock -1.03%. Returns have not by themselves lifted this stock at H1 when paired with a mixed P&L.
findings.why_not_priced: Not announced and not certain (probability perhaps a third to a half); a priced buyback would show in a pre-print run-in, and the stock instead fell about 3% over the two sessions before the print. Last year's programme is in the filings and so the pattern is visible, which is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: Last year's buyback notice https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20251030/140120251029581879.pdf; Mizuho stake report https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=2002&b=n202610070394 (2026-10-07). Different documents, same thesis.

findings.finding: The 中食・惣菜 segment (Tokatsu Foods, supplier to Seven-Eleven) was already down 33% in Q1 OP (1.0bn vs 1.4bn) and 7-Eleven Japan's July existing-store traffic fell 2.2% (June -3.5%), so this segment likely drags Q2 again against a FY plan of 5.7bn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated history; the segment weakness was part of the Q1 that fell 4.78%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: 7-Eleven monthly data are public and Q1 already showed the drop; it matters only net of the rest of the company (5.7bn of 46bn plan, ~12%), and the FX tailwind on overseas (37.8%) is larger.

outside_window.finding: Domestic flour price pass-through of the +12% October wheat sale price lands from 2027-01 deliveries; the Oct-Dec cost lag and its recovery show in Q3/Q4 results, not this print except via guidance wording.
中期経営計画2026 ends this fiscal year (FY27/3); its 57bn OP target is abandoned in the 46bn guide, and a new plan with capital-allocation targets is likely with the FY print in May 2027.

baseline_tension: Lean is -0.14 and the free control mildly negative (+3.25% 20d run-up, partly unwound over the last two sessions); findings net slightly positive. Strongest positive the release could carry: a new buyback plus a held FY guide with H1 on plan, which I looked for and sized; strongest negative: a FY trim on oil, and this name's habit of selling in-line prints (-3.5%, -4.8% at the last two). Net: no edge beyond a coin flip.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (negative on a public series): cost/oil guidance finding -0.3 -> -0.2 and the 中食/7-Eleven monthly finding -0.2 -> -0.1, since both rest on public series; kept non-zero only because the release can ADD a forecast decision.
Rule 1/2 in the scaled number: p_up 50 -> 52, the negatives being public and the positive (buyback) having been looked for and found plausible.
Rule 2: negatives (2) do not outnumber positives (2); the strongest positive is written in baseline_tension. Nothing else changed.
